issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1(iii) requires the KL inequality for every x in the open set Omega, which strictly contains X = [1,2] in Example 1. For x in Omega\X, partial Psi(x) is empty, so dist = infinity and L(x) is the set of all non-maximizers. The condition is therefore a global KL condition at such x. In Example 1, for any x > 0 (e.g. x slightly above 2), y = pi is a stationary point with phi*(x) - phi(x,pi) = x(sqrt2/2 + 1) > 0, so KL fails there. Example 1 therefore violates Assumption 1. The same mechanism makes the assumption non-local near the boundary of any non-open X, contrary to the claims that it is 'significantly weaker' and only requires KL for x in dom p.

failure_location.quote: For example, the minimax problem in Example~\eqref{example} satisfies the local KL condition but not the global one.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw or correct the claims about Example 1 and the scope of the assumption. Alternatively, reformulate (iii) so it is required only for x in X, or with a finite level set outside X, and re-prove the openness and differentiability arguments (Lemma lem:open, Lemma lem:diff_ext, Theorem thm:Phi_smooth) at boundary points of X.
issues.overall_effect: The theorems remain conditional on Assumption 1, but they do not apply to the paper's motivating example or to similar constrained problems with spurious inner stationary points. The advertised broader applicability is unsupported.
issues.title: Assumption 1(iii) imposes global KL on Omega\X, so the motivating Example 1 is not covered
issues.why_classification: The formal results survive as stated, but the main advertised scope is lost. Restoring it needs a modified assumption plus a contained new differentiability argument near the boundary of X.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 2 loops indefinitely and returns nothing. (eps,r)-stationarity requires dist(0, partial Psi) near the iterate, which involves the unavailable gradient of F*, so it cannot be checked. The proofs only show by contradiction that some iterate with index at most K_hat is stationary. Later iterates may leave the stationary region, so neither the last iterate nor x^{ell(K_hat)} is certified. The claimed complexity 'for computing' a stationary point therefore has no computable output behind it.

failure_location.quote: Then Algorithm~\ref{algo_implement:whole} generates a pair $(x^k, y^k)$ in at most $\widehat{K}_\epsilon$ iterations such that $x^k$ is an $(\epsilon, \gamma \epsilon^\sigma/(4L_f))$-stationary point

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantees as 'some iterate among the first K_hat is (eps,r)-stationary'. Alternatively, add a computable output rule with a proof that the selected iterate is stationary.
issues.overall_effect: The iteration and oracle complexity bounds certify existence of a good iterate, not that the procedure computes or identifies one. The numerical protocol (returning the last iterate) is not covered by the theory.
issues.title: Algorithm 2 has no stopping rule or output; guarantees only assert an unidentified stationary iterate
issues.why_classification: The bounds themselves stand, but the guarantee must be weakened to an existence statement, or a new selection argument must be supplied.
